readme: One list of adversarial safetensors files. Every reader (qd_export::SafeTensorsFile, qd_metal::SafeTensors, qd_train.memory) must give `expect` on each case. Build each file as: u64-LE length prefix, header bytes, data_len zero bytes. header = the header text (UTF-8); pad_header_to = if set, append spaces until the header is this many bytes (still valid JSON); header_len = if set, the length prefix instead of the header's real byte length; truncate_to = if set, cut the finished file to this many bytes. rust_error_contains = a substring both Rust readers' error must hold (Python matches on the refusal alone, not the text). header_encoding = if "utf-16-le", the header text is written as UTF-16 little-endian bytes instead of UTF-8 (the prefix is its byte length).

cases.name: valid_one_tensor
cases.why: baseline: the smallest real file

cases.name: valid_space_padded_header
cases.why: the writer pads the header with spaces to an 8-byte boundary

cases.name: valid_header_exactly_64_mib
cases.why: the bound is inclusive

cases.name: header_64_mib_plus_one
cases.why: one byte past the bound

cases.name: header_65_mib
cases.why: a header the old 100 MiB bound accepted

cases.name: length_prefix_u64_max
cases.why: oversized declared length on a tiny file

cases.name: zero_length_header
cases.why: an empty tensor set is not a model; the old qd-metal reader accepted it

cases.name: length_past_end_of_file
cases.why: declared header longer than the file

cases.name: file_shorter_than_length_prefix
cases.why: 3 bytes: no room for the u64

cases.name: file_truncated_inside_header
cases.why: cut 10 bytes in, mid header

cases.name: data_section_shorter_than_offsets
cases.why: offsets claim 8 bytes, the file holds 4

cases.name: offsets_out_of_bounds
cases.why: a tensor whose end is past the data section

cases.name: offsets_end_before_begin
cases.why: reversed range

cases.name: overlapping_offsets
cases.why: two tensors sharing bytes

cases.name: offsets_disagree_with_shape
cases.why: 2 x F32 = 8 bytes but the range spans 4

cases.name: shape_product_overflows
cases.why: element count overflows usize

cases.name: negative_shape_entry
cases.why: shape entries are unsigned

cases.name: data_offsets_wrong_arity
cases.why: one offset instead of two

cases.name: missing_dtype
cases.why: entry without a dtype

cases.name: unknown_dtype
cases.why: a dtype the format does not name

cases.name: header_not_json
cases.why: text that is not JSON

cases.name: header_json_array
cases.why: JSON, but not an object

cases.name: header_utf16_le
cases.why: a UTF-16 header; python's json.loads(bytes) auto-detects the encoding, serde_json does not

cases.name: header_utf8_bom
cases.why: a byte-order mark before the object; python's json.loads(bytes) skipped it, serde_json refuses

cases.name: nan_in_metadata
cases.why: NaN is not JSON; python's json.loads accepts it by default

cases.name: zero_product_shape_overflows_first
cases.why: the element count overflows usize before the trailing 0: Rust folds left to right with checked_mul, so a final zero does not rescue it; python's math.prod returned 0

cases.name: json_nesting_127_deep
cases.why: serde_json refuses the 128th nested container (recursion limit 128); this is 127 (the object, __metadata__, 125 arrays)

cases.name: json_nesting_128_deep
cases.why: the 128th nested container: serde_json's recursion limit; python's json parses it (its own limit is ~1000)

cases.name: number_literal_overflows_to_infinity
cases.why: 1e400 is out of range for serde_json; python's json.loads returns inf
